accepted_decisions_read.title: Copilot CLI adapter uses bounded prompt-file context injection

decision.chosen: Keep Copilot CLI prompt composition inside the Copilot adapter/provider boundary, build the Architect envelope with context-economy controls, retain a bounded history window, mark the current turn explicitly, and fall back to a temporary prompt.md file when the serialized prompt exceeds the safe argv byte budget. Surface prompt byte count, history count, advertised MCP server/tool count, current-turn marker status, and model selection to the Context Inspector.

alternatives.option: Pass the full prompt exclusively through argv
alternatives.rejected_because: Large Architect prompts can exceed shell or process argument limits, especially on Windows, and fail before Copilot CLI starts.

alternatives.option: Move Copilot prompt serialization into Architect core
alternatives.rejected_because: That would contaminate provider-neutral core contracts with a provider-specific CLI transport concern.

alternatives.option: Rely only on MCP tools and omit serialized task/history context
alternatives.rejected_because: The CLI still needs the concrete current turn, autonomy/reporting contracts, and bounded conversation context before it can decide which MCP tools to call.

guard_rails: Do not move Copilot CLI prompt serialization or prompt.md fallback into provider-neutral Architect core.
Do not remove the explicit current-turn marker from Copilot CLI prompts without replacing it with an equally strong active-turn isolation mechanism.
Do not disable bounded history or argv byte budgeting for Copilot CLI runs.
Do not treat serialized prompt context as authoritative graph truth; repository facts still require DreamGraph MCP grounding.

accepted_decisions_read.title: Standalone Architect CLI adapters execute through a daemon MCP bridge

decision.chosen: Standalone Architect chat requests with adapter codex-cli or copilot-cli now invoke a daemon-owned CLI bridge. The bridge materializes per-run CLI home/config files, exposes the active daemon MCP endpoint to the selected CLI through a stdio MCP proxy, audits tool calls, and returns normalized content, route, provenance, and tool trace metadata. Metadata-only fallback is no longer used for selected CLI chat execution.

alternatives.option: Keep codex-cli and copilot-cli selector values as metadata-only deterministic fallbacks.
alternatives.rejected_because: That was the reported bug and made UI/runtime/provenance metadata claim an adapter path that was not actually used.

alternatives.option: Spawn a fresh DreamGraph stdio server directly for each CLI run.
alternatives.rejected_because: That can create a second graph/session boundary instead of using the active daemon session.

alternatives.option: Let CLI adapters use provider-native filesystem and shell tools for repository operations.
alternatives.rejected_because: That bypasses DreamGraph MCP authority and weakens auditability.

guard_rails: Do not reintroduce metadata-only fallback for selected codex-cli or copilot-cli chat execution.
Do not let standalone CLI adapters answer repository questions without a reachable DreamGraph MCP bridge or an explicit fail-closed error.
Do not route CLI repository mutations through provider-native shell/write/read surfaces when DreamGraph MCP tools are available.
Do not spawn a separate graph-authority session for CLI runs without a new ADR that addresses active daemon runtime identity.
Keep CLI adapter route, runtime, provenance, and tool trace metadata synchronized with ADR-216.
